text:
alex: FYI sales handed over DataFlowX for a large POC — they pushed back on our CAIQ answers. Need quick clarifications to unblock pricing/contract.
maria: thanks — which items are failing?
alex: mainly encryption-in-transit/key management, sub-processors list, and on-prem connector details. Customer asked for a network diagram and that DataFlowX can be deployed in a private VPC.
josh: do we already have a vendor pack from them?
maria: I pulled the initial packet into the intake form: https://vendors.redwood.internal/intake/DFX-332 - it has a redacted SOC2 cert but no pen test or ISO statement.
vendor-intake-bot: New vendor intake submitted: DataFlowX (DFX-332). Checklist status: CAIQ incomplete, SOC2 present (type II redacted), Subprocessors missing.
sam: can they support SAML + IdP-initiated SSO? Customer requires SCIM provisioning too.
alex: sales says yes for SAML but SCIM is on roadmap. Need confirmation and timeline.
emily: on the encryption question — they list TLS 1.2+ and AES-256 at rest. But our legal wanted KMS/HSM details and whether customer keys are supported.
josh: ask them: 1) do they support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key / KMS/HSM) for hosted offering? 2) If not, do they support key isolation for Dedicated/VPC?
maria: I can draft the ask. Also need to know retention for logs and what PII they store. Customer is explicit: no raw logs outside EU.
alex: action: maria to request network diagram and deployment options; josh to ask about keys and pen test; emily to confirm data retention and subprocessors. Sam to confirm SSO/SCIM timeline.
maria: draft sent to DataFlowX support@dataflowx.com: "Hi — we need: CAIQ gaps list, network/topology diagram for private VPC deploy, deployment matrix (hosted/dedicated/on-prem), SOC2 full report, pen test summary, subprocessor list (locations), data retention policy, and KMS/HSM/customer-key options. Can you confirm SCIM availability/timeline?"
vendor-intake-bot: Note added to ticket DFX-332 by maria.
DataFlowX Support: Thanks for the detailed list — we can provide the network diagram and subprocessor list today. SOC2 full report requires an NDA (link: https://dfx-secure.example/nda). SCIM is slated for Q3; we can provide interim SCIM-like provisioning via API. Regarding CMK: hosted offering does not support BYOK today; Dedicated/VPC customers can bring keys via our KMS integration (AWS KMS & GCP KMS).
emily: they require NDA for SOC2 — fine, legal can do quick sig. CMK answer is borderline but acceptable if Dedicated supports BYOK. Customer leaning Dedicated anyway.
josh: ask for pen test scope and most recent date. Also request redacted vuln summary if possible.
DataFlowX Support: Pen test conducted 2025-09-12 by SecureProbe. We can share a redacted executive summary.
sam: SCIM roadmap Q3 is ok if we can do API provisioning for POC. Sales needs a one-pager that explains: SAML ok, SCIM planned Q3, API provisioning details. I'll draft.
maria: DataFlowX shared network diagram attachment (uploaded to ticket). It's a high-level diagram showing public-hosted flow and a private-VPC peering option with a connector appliance for on-prem. They also included a config snippet for the connector.
DataFlowX Support: Connector config sample: ```yaml
connector:
  mode: vpn
  allowed_cidrs: ["10.0.0.0/16"]
  auth: token
```
alex: can someone verify the connector uses mTLS between appliance and service? customer requires mutual auth.
emily: diagram notes TLS mutual auth for the connector and token for initial registration. Need to confirm cert rotation cadence.
josh: DataFlowX — please confirm mTLS for connector and cert rotation policy. Also confirm if connector can be scoped to EU-only egress.
DataFlowX Support: Connector uses mTLS (mutual TLS) and certificates rotate every 90 days. Egress can be restricted to specific regions (EU).
maria: good. Subprocessors list attached includes AWS (eu-west-1), GCP (europe-west4), and analytics provider in US (opt-out available).
emily: opt-out for analytics is important — ask if analytics can be disabled for enterprise customers by default.
DataFlowX Support: Analytics can be disabled per-tenant and will be off for enterprise POCs.
sam: on pricing/blocker side — customer asked for a short SLA for Dedicated: target latency and uptime. Sales wants this in writing for contract.
alex: we can draft an interim SLA tied to Dedicated offering numbers they published on website, but legal wants vendor confirmation that those figures apply to customer with dedicated capacity.
josh: DataFlowX — can you confirm SLA for Dedicated customers (target p95 latency, availability %) and whether credits apply for breaches?
DataFlowX Support: We commit to 99.9% uptime for Dedicated and p95 latency 200ms for 512 tokens; credits apply as per contract. We'll provide the formal SLA PDF.
maria: perfect. We have most answers. Remaining items: pen test redacted summary, SOC2 NDA, confirmed BYOK for Dedicated, cert rotation cadence (provided), analytics opt-out (confirmed), SCIM timeline + API provisioning details.
emily: legal will review SOC2 NDA and should be able to sign within 48 hours.
sam: sales — I'll prepare a one-pager and POC runbook with the connector setup steps and caveats (no BYOK for hosted).
alex: timeline: get NDA & SOC2, pen test exec summary, and BYOK confirmation for Dedicated. If all good, push to procurement and we can sign POC contract by EOW.
josh: I'll follow up on pen test and BYOK confirmation, pinging them in 24h.
maria: noted. Adding final checklist to ticket and tagging @legal and @sales-lead.
vendor-intake-bot: Ticket DFX-332 updated: checklist advanced to 'awaiting-nda'.
alex: thanks everyone — close the loop in 48h. :thumbsup:
